entry: Not decided; recorded so neither answer below is read as final. Asked whether every picture should need a sign-in, the owner said: "Yes, every picture requires sign in." Later the same day: "I just realized what pictures requiring sign-in means. I don't care if static assets like posters or images of actors are public assets. Although I think if we're having S3 be a potential storage solution, pre-signed URLs is a common case for that. But if we're already fetching them from a public place to populate them, then I don't see why we could just do that." The lead then asked whether pictures that are frames of the films themselves (generated posters, chapter pictures, scrub previews) need a sign-in; that question is unanswered. Until it is, no design locks picture access.
